title: The connected components of the affine line over a base
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $B$ be a nonempty $k$-scheme whose structure morphism
$B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and of finite type
[def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathbf A^1_B=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_B(\mathcal O_B[t])$ be the affine line of [def-sbc-affine-space], let
$s_0:B\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_B$ be the zero section, the closed
immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] defined by $t=0$, and let
$\mathbf G_{m,B}=\mathbf A^1_B\setminus s_0(B)$ be the complement of
the zero section. Let $1:B\to\mathbf A^1_B$ be the unit section,
the section defined by $t=1$ of the projection, which factors through
$\mathbf G_{m,B}$.

1. The connected components of $\mathbf A^1_B$, and those of
$\mathbf G_{m,B}$, are exactly the inverse images of the
connected components of $B$.
1. Every connected component of $\mathbf A^1_B$ meets
$\mathbf G_{m,B}$, and meets the image of the unit section
$1$.
1. Every connected component of $\mathbf G_{m,B}$ meets the image
of the unit section $1$.

Here a connected component means a maximal nonempty connected subset of the underlying topological space, with connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme].

proof.text: Write $X=\mathbf A^1_B$, $G=\mathbf G_{m,B}$, $p:X\to B$ and $q=p|_G:G\to B$. The projection $p$ is smooth of relative dimension one by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. The forward implication of [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] therefore makes $p$ flat and locally of finite presentation. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] to conclude that $p$ is open. No smoothness, flatness or finite-presentation assertion about $q$ is needed.

The subset $G$ is open in $X$ because it is the complement of the closed image of $s_0$. If $O$ is open in $G$, then $O$ is open in $X$, so $q(O)=p(O)$ is open in $B$. Thus $q$ is open too. The unit section satisfies $p(1(y))=y$ and takes values in $G$, so both $p$ and $q$ are surjective. Both maps are continuous, being underlying maps of scheme morphisms.

source.place: Proof Step 1 (open complement) and Step 3 (unit section)

proof.text: For $y\in B$ put $K=\kappa(y)$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the topological fibre of $p$ is homeomorphic to the underlying space of $X\times_B\operatorname{Spec}K$. Using the fibre-product definition of affine space in [def-sbc-affine-space], this scheme is canonically $\mathbf A^1_{\operatorname{Spec}K}=\operatorname{Spec}(K[t])$. Explicitly, a map into $(B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[t])\times_B\operatorname{Spec}K$ is a compatible pair of maps into $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[t]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K$; the map into $B$ is forced by the latter. These are exactly the pairs defining $\operatorname{Spec}K\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[t]$, so [def-pc-fibre-product] supplies mutually inverse maps. The affine-base formula in [def-sbc-affine-space] gives $\operatorname{Spec}(K[t])$.

source.place: Tag 01M0, definition-affine-n-space and following base-change formula; also schemes.tex Tags 01K0 (definition-fibre), 01K1 (lemma-fibre-topological)

proof.text: Every fibre of $p$ is connected. Indeed, in the polynomial ring of [def-weil-polynomial-ring], the coefficient in degree $\deg F+\deg H$ of the product of two nonzero polynomials over the field $K$ is the product of their nonzero leading coefficients. It is nonzero by the field axioms [def-weil-field], so $K[t]$ is a domain and its zero ideal is prime. In the Zariski topology on the spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a closed set $V(I)$ containing this zero prime has $I\subseteq(0)$ and hence is the entire spectrum. Thus the zero prime is dense and belongs to every nonempty open subset. A partition into two nonempty opens is impossible since both would contain it; this proves connectedness in [def-weil-connected-scheme], including nonemptiness.

source.place: definition-spectrum-ring and definition of the Zariski topology; Tag 030A (lemma-polynomial-domain-normal), with the elementary polynomial-domain argument written out

proof.text: Every fibre of $q$ is the open subspace $G\cap p^{-1}(y)$ of the fibre of $p$. It contains $1(y)$, so it is nonempty. Any nonempty open subset of this open subspace is open and nonempty in $p^{-1}(y)$, and therefore contains the dense zero prime from Step 4. Two nonempty disjoint opens of $q^{-1}(y)$ cannot exist. Consequently all fibres of $q$ are connected in the sense of [def-weil-connected-scheme]. This argument needs no localization-domain theorem and applies over every residue field, not only at closed points.

source.place: Proof Step 1, connectedness of punctured-line fibres, with the generic-point argument written out

proof.text: Let $f$ be either $p$ or $q$, and let $D\subseteq B$ be a connected component. For the restriction $f_D:f^{-1}(D)\to D$, every relative open has the form $f^{-1}(D)\cap O$ for $O$ open in the source of $f$, and its image is $D\cap f(O)$. Hence $f_D$ is an open continuous surjection. If $f_D^{-1}(T)$ is closed, its open complement has image exactly $D\setminus T$, by surjectivity; openness of $f_D$ makes $T$ closed in $D$. The converse follows from continuity. Thus $D$ has the quotient topology under $f_D$. Its fibres are exactly the connected fibres proved in Steps 4 and 5.

source.place: Tag 0378 (lemma-connected-fibres-connected-components), quotient-topology hypothesis of Tag 0377 written out for the restriction to D

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-connected-fibres-quotient-preimage-connected] with $P=f^{-1}(D)$, $W=D$ and $h=f_D$. Step 6 verifies continuity, all fibres connected, and the equivalence between closedness and closedness of the preimage. The whole space $T=W=D$ is closed in itself and is nonempty and connected because $D$ is a connected component. The lemma therefore proves that $f^{-1}(D)$ is connected. This use does not require $D$ to be open or even closed in $B$.

source.place: Tag 0377, lemma-connected-fibres-quotient-topology-connected-components, applied to f_D and the closed subset T=W

proof.text: The connected set $E=f^{-1}(D)$ is maximal connected. To see this, let $C$ be a connected subset containing $E$. A separation of $f(C)$ into two nonempty relative opens would pull back to a separation of $C$, so $f(C)$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Surjectivity over $D$ gives $D\subseteq f(C)$, and maximality of $D$ forces $f(C)=D$. Thus $C\subseteq f^{-1}(D)=E$, as required.

source.place: Tag 0376 (lemma-image-connected-space), elementary proof of connectedness of the image; Tag 004S (definition-connected-components)

proof.text: These are all the components of the source of $f$. For completeness, every $y\in B$ belongs to a component: take the union $D_y$ of all connected subsets containing $y$. In a separation of this union, each such subset lies in the side containing $y$, so the other side is empty; hence $D_y$ is connected and is maximal by its construction [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Now let $C$ be a component of the source and take $x\in C$, $y=f(x)$. Step 7 gives the connected set $E=f^{-1}(D_y)$ containing $x$. The union $C\cup E$ is connected, because in a separation both connected subsets must lie on the side containing their common point $x$. Maximality of $C$ and of $E$ (Step 8) yields $C=E$. Applying this for $p$ and $q$ proves clause (1).

source.place: Tag 004T, lemma-connected-components, union-of-connected-subsets proof written out; blueprint proof Step 2

proof.text: For any component $D$ of $B$, choose $y\in D$, which is possible by nonempty connectedness. The point $1(y)$ belongs to $G$ and satisfies $p(1(y))=q(1(y))=y$. Therefore it lies in the corresponding components $p^{-1}(D)$ and $q^{-1}(D)$. The component description already proved implies that every component of $X$ meets both $G$ and the image of $1$, and every component of $G$ meets the image of $1$. These are exactly clauses (2) and (3).
